newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends 1/2 U.S. cent lower after RB easing.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends 1/2 U.S. cent lower after RB easing.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended a busy session on Thursday half a U.S. cent lower after the Reserve Bank said it wanted easier conditions.
Dealers said the local market was still long and they predict a further move down, initially to US$0.6980 and then to more solid support level at 0.6950.
At 5.00 p.m. (0400 GMT) the Kiwi was near its lows for the day at 0.7001/08.

The Kiwi fell quickly from 0.7049/56, where it stood just before the Reserve Bank's six monthly economic forecasts were published in the morning, while the Trade-Weighted Index fell initially to 68.48 from 69.04.
The TWI ended at 68.60, still well above the 68.0 level the bank assumed in its economic forecasts.
A dealer said locals were looking to defend long positions established on expectations of a hold-the-line statement against U.S. sellers and new selling out of Asia.
"I don't think we have seen the last of the selling," said one Wellington dealer.
He predicted something of a shakeout, although he stressed the Kiwi was in no danger of plummeting.
He doubted interest rates would fall very far and they would continue to underpin the currency.
RB Governor Don Brash surprised markets in his statement when he said conditions were inappropriately firm and he wanted them to return to December levels.
